prose.comp_lead: IndiaMART, not a factory, is the strongest competitor: it holds 25 of the 160 top-10 places across 16 target searches. Among manufacturers, Divine meets NK Polycross (on the same Rupal–Bavla road), Shalimar, Frank Industries and Amrut Plastopack most often.
comp_analysis: There are two different battles. For local searches (Ahmedabad, Gujarat, Rupal–Bavla), 42–50% of the top 10 are marketplace and directory list pages: IndiaMART city pages, Justdial "top manufacturers" lists and TradeIndia. A factory site rarely beats a list page there, so the play is to be inside those lists with a strong profile. For national product searches the picture flips. 70% of the top 10 for "multilayer tarpaulin" are manufacturer product pages, and 60% for LDPE tarpaulin. That's where Divine's own pages can win.

The closest rival is 4 km away. NK Polycross sits on the same Rupal–Bavla road, makes 70–300 GSM multilayer sheets and ponchos, and owns the "rupal bavla" search through its IndiaMART profile. It has 4.5★ from 42 Google reviews against Divine's 3.7★ from 6, an IndiaMART rating of 4.7 and a YouTube channel. But it shows no prices, no minimum order and no blog, and much of its product-page wording matches Supreme Industries' copy. Original spec tables, open prices and more reviews beat it.

Frank Industries is running the same playbook as you. The Ahmedabad firm ranks in the top 10 for 6 of the 16 searches with two city blog posts, including "Best Rain Poncho Manufacturers in Ahmedabad". Its posts carry no prices, weights or GSM data, its site is dated, and IndiaMART lists its poncho line under "trader". Divine already outranks it for "rain poncho manufacturer in gujarat" (#2 against #5). Factory proof and real numbers widen that lead.

Price is an open goal. Two whole clusters are about price. Divine has no page for "tarpaulin price per kg" (a critical mismatch: nothing on the site states a price), and priced product pages win "90 GSM tarpaulin". Amrut Plastopack is #1 for "multilayer tarpaulin manufacturer in india" partly because every listing shows a price (₹169–188/kg). A price band per GSM is the biggest single content gap against competitors.
prose.aud_lead: The research found 15 buyer segments and 6 personas. Dealers and distributors are the most valuable and the easiest to reach. Pilgrimage and seva buyers already fit the ₹20 poncho best. Every persona scores lowest on trust.
aud_analysis: Dealers first. A dealer buying for a district or a network of shops is worth more than any single end buyer. They order before the season, in February to May, and look for a Gujarat source on IndiaMART and Google. Today the site gives a dealer nothing to work with: no dealers page, no price basis, no standard minimum order and no freight terms. A dealers page in English, Hindi and Gujarati is the most valuable page Divine doesn't have.

Ponchos sell to occasions. The strongest poncho buyers are yatra seva committees and route vendors (Kedarnath alone had a record 16.52 lakh pilgrims in 2025), plus festival committees, theme parks, municipalities and schools. Most order in March to May. The ₹20* price already matches what route buyers pay. What's missing is carton quantity, colour mix per carton, dispatch time and what the asterisk means.

Tarpaulin buyers are afraid of being cheated. The most common complaints are sheets lighter than the GSM claimed, confusion between price per kg and per piece, sheets going brittle in the sun, and HDPE-vs-LDPE confusion. Each one becomes a page or a table: weight per sheet for every size and GSM, a "check the GSM at delivery" guide, a stated weight tolerance, and an LDPE-multilayer-vs-HDPE explainer that says plainly Divine makes no HDPE.

Trust is the weakest score for every persona, with totals from 35 to 63 out of 100. Named people, factory video, real customer stories and more Google reviews lift every persona at once, which is why they lead the action plan.
prose.dem_lead: This section uses real Google Trends data for India (monthly, 2019 onwards). Tarpaulin sells all year with a June peak; raincoats spike sharply in July. Bulk buyers order 6–10 weeks before both.
dem_analysis: Tarpaulin never goes quiet. Search interest bottoms out in January at 59% of its June peak, climbs from March, then jumps to 87 in May and 100 in June. Harvests add a second wave for grain covers: rabi in March–May, kharif in October–November. The Hindi word "tirpal" grew 76% between 2019 and 2025, so Hindi pages are a growing way in.

Raincoats sell in a short window. Interest sits at 9–11 from November to April, rises to 33 in May and 88 in June, and peaks at 100 in July. Bulk buyers (dealers, municipalities, schools, yatra committees) order before that curve, so poncho campaigns must be live by April.

Say "raincoat", not only "poncho". "Rain poncho" gets almost no searches in India, and "poncho" on its own peaks in December as a winter-fashion word. The poncho pages should lead with "plastic raincoat", "raincoat poncho" and "disposable raincoat" in titles and headings, keeping "poncho" as the product name.

Schemes help; most tenders don't fit. Gujarat's tadpatri sahay yojana (i-Khedut) pays farmers 50–75% of a tarpaulin's cost in a two-week February window, and has no supplier empanelment. That makes it a reason to publish a Gujarati explainer and stock Gujarat dealers before February, not a sales channel. Most GeM tarpaulin tenders specify woven HDPE sheets to IS 7903, which Divine doesn't make. Rajasthan's manufacturer EOI asks for multilayer, cross-laminated, UV-stabilised sheets, which matches Divine's product and is worth checking.
prose.auth_lead: Of the 11 companies compared, Divine has the youngest domain, the fewest reviews and no marketplace listings. The competitors that rank locally all have IndiaMART storefronts, and most have YouTube.
auth_analysis: Every serious rival is on IndiaMART; Divine isn't. Seven of the ten Indian competitors have IndiaMART storefronts: Everest Polymers has 146 ratings at 4.2, and NK Polycross is rated 4.7. IndiaMART pages appear in all four AI-style "best manufacturer" searches. With no IndiaMART, TradeIndia or ExportersIndia listing, Divine is invisible where most bulk buyers compare suppliers, and in the sources AI assistants quote.

The Google Business Profile is working against you. The address reads "710-711Village Rupal Rupal ,", the category is "Business to business service" rather than a tarpaulin or plastic-products category, and there are only 6 reviews. Divine isn't in the top 20 Maps results for "tarpaulin manufacturer Bavla Ahmedabad", while NK Polycross, 4 km away, has 42 reviews. Fixing the category and address and reaching 25 reviews is the fastest local win available.

Listings disagree about who Divine is. Justdial says "Divine Fab Tech" in "Adroda" and shows three different ratings. A JD Mart product is titled "200 gsm HDPE tarpaulin". The site links to a Facebook share redirect instead of the page itself. Local search and AI assistants trust listings that agree on name, address and phone.
prose.win_lead: Divine can't outspend IndiaMART or outlast Supreme. It can be the most transparent, most local and easiest-to-find factory in its niche: LDPE multilayer tarpaulins and bulk raincoat-ponchos from Bavla.
prose.camp_lead: Ten campaigns over twelve months, timed to the Trends curves and the buying calendar. Each one says what to run, for whom, on which channels, and how to measure it.

win.title: Win the Bavla–Ahmedabad map
win.body: List pages and the map pack win local searches. Fix the Business Profile (address, tarpaulin and raincoat categories, products, photos), make Justdial match, and reach 25+ reviews to close the gap with NK Polycross. Then get inside the lists: the IndiaMART, Justdial and TradeIndia Ahmedabad categories.
moves: 25 Google reviews by end of January

win.title: Publish what rivals hide
win.body: NK Polycross, Frank, A.U. and Supreme show no prices; Amrut wins partly because it does. Publish price bands per GSM, weight per sheet for every stock size, a GSM tolerance, carton quantities and lead times. That answers the top buyer complaint (GSM shortfall) and fills the "price per kg" cluster nobody owns.

win.title: Speak the way buyers search
win.body: Say "raincoat" where buyers say raincoat, and "tirpal" or "tadpatri" where they say those. Add Gujarati and Hindi versions of the farmer, trader and dealer pages. No competitor in the top 10 has them, and searches for "tirpal" grew 76% in six years.

win.title: Show the factory
win.body: Trust is every persona's weakest score. Name the owners (A.U. Industries does), state a daily capacity (Aashi Rainwear's "8,000 raincoats daily" post ranks for poncho searches), post factory videos (NK Polycross and Everest are on YouTube) and add real customer stories. That turns a new domain into a credible supplier.

win.title: Build a dealer network
win.body: Dealers are the most valuable and easiest-to-reach segment, and they order in February to May. A dealers page with price basis, standard minimum order, freight and margin, plus a WhatsApp catalogue, turns one search into a district's worth of repeat orders.

win.title: Arrive before the season
win.body: Raincoat demand peaks in July and tarpaulin in June, but bulk buyers decide 6–10 weeks earlier. Every seasonal page and campaign goes live by April. Approach yatra committees in March, and update harvest-cover content before March and before October.
moves: Harvest pages before Mar and Oct

campaigns.name: Monsoon raincoat bulk push
campaigns.why: Raincoat searches climb from 33 in May to 100 in July, and dealers, municipalities and schools buy before the peak.
campaigns.audience: Dealers and retailers, municipal and school buyers, construction and factory HR
campaigns.channels: SEO landing pages, Google Ads on "raincoat bulk" terms, IndiaMART, WhatsApp broadcast to dealers
campaigns.content: Price-by-quantity table from ₹20*, carton quantity, colour mix and dispatch time, with "plastic raincoat" wording
campaigns.kpi: Poncho leads per week in GA4, cost per lead, IndiaMART enquiries

campaigns.name: Yatra and seva ponchos
campaigns.why: Kedarnath opens in spring (16.52 lakh pilgrims in 2025), and Amarnath, Kanwar, Rath Yatra and Pandharpur follow in June–August. Seva committees and route vendors buy in bulk at around the ₹20 price.
campaigns.audience: Yatra seva committees, dharamshalas, route vendors, travel operators
campaigns.channels: Hindi landing page, WhatsApp outreach to committees and trusts, a YouTube short of a carton being packed, Justdial
campaigns.content: A Hindi "yatra raincoat bulk" page: a carton of 100 with its colour mix, and delivery times to the Haridwar, Rishikesh and Jammu routes
campaigns.kpi: Committee enquiries, orders by route, repeat orders next year

campaigns.name: Pre-monsoon tarpaulin
campaigns.why: Tarpaulin interest climbs to 87 in May and 100 in June as contractors, transporters and households cover up before the rains.
campaigns.channels: SEO (truck cover, monsoon shed and construction guides), Google Ads, YouTube, WhatsApp
campaigns.content: Size and GSM calculator, weight per sheet, eyelet and rope guidance, monsoon-shed kit sizes
campaigns.kpi: Tarpaulin leads by use case, calculator uses

campaigns.name: Harvest covers
campaigns.why: The rabi harvest (March–May) and kharif procurement (October–November) leave grain in the open just when unseasonal rain hits.
campaigns.audience: Mandi traders, FPOs, cold storage and warehouses
campaigns.channels: Gujarati and Hindi pages, the grain-storage guide, WhatsApp to APMC traders, Justdial
campaigns.content: A "large sizes in stock" table (30×40 ft and up) with dispatch times, recommending 150–200 GSM
campaigns.kpi: Large-size orders, repeat buyers per season

campaigns.name: Tadpatri sahay explainer
campaigns.why: Gujarat farmers claim 50–75% back on up to 2 sheets through i-Khedut, in a two-week February window.
campaigns.audience: Gujarat farmers and the dealers who sell to them
campaigns.channels: Gujarati page, dealer WhatsApp, a Gujarati YouTube video
campaigns.content: A Gujarati explainer covering how to claim, which GSM to buy and where the dealers are; stock Gujarat dealers in January
campaigns.kpi: Gujarati page visits, dealer orders in January–February

campaigns.name: Dealer network drive
campaigns.why: Dealers are the highest-value segment, and they stock up in February–May.
campaigns.audience: Tarpaulin and rainwear dealers in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
campaigns.channels: Dealers page (English, Hindi, Gujarati), IndiaMART, TradeIndia, WhatsApp Business catalogue, trade associations
campaigns.content: Price basis, standard minimum order, freight, dealer margin and a sample kit
campaigns.kpi: New dealers signed, dealer reorder rate

campaigns.name: Reviews and listings sprint
campaigns.why: Divine has 6 Google reviews to NK Polycross's 42, and no IndiaMART, TradeIndia or ExportersIndia listing.
campaigns.audience: Past buyers, and buyers browsing the marketplaces
campaigns.channels: WhatsApp review requests, Business Profile, IndiaMART, TradeIndia, ExportersIndia, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect
campaigns.content: A short review link, a photo of each dispatched order, and listings that all show the same name, address and phone
campaigns.kpi: 25 Google reviews by end of January, listings live, Maps rank for "tarpaulin manufacturer Bavla"

campaigns.name: Factory on camera
campaigns.why: Trust is every persona's weakest score, and rivals with YouTube channels (NK Polycross, Everest) look established.
campaigns.audience: All buyers, plus AI assistants that cite YouTube
campaigns.channels: YouTube, Instagram reels, embedded on the product pages
campaigns.content: Six films: the lamination line, a GSM weigh test, poncho stitching, packing a carton, dispatch, the colour range

campaigns.name: Branded ponchos for companies
campaigns.why: Corporate and CSR buyers pay about ₹65 a piece for logo-printed ponchos (MOQ 200 on the marketplaces). Run this only if you offer printing.
campaigns.audience: Brand and HR managers, CSR teams, event agencies
campaigns.channels: LinkedIn company page and outreach, a landing page, Google Ads
campaigns.content: A "custom printed raincoat-ponchos" page with the print area and MOQ, plus a mock-up sent on WhatsApp within 24 hours

campaigns.name: Festival and pandal covers
campaigns.why: Ganesh Chaturthi pandals (September) and Navratri garba (September–October) need covers and rain gear while the monsoon withdraws.
campaigns.audience: Pandal decorators, tent houses, festival committees
campaigns.channels: Justdial, WhatsApp to tent houses, local Instagram
campaigns.content: Pandal cover sizes, quick-delivery stock, raincoat packs for committees
